title: Understanding Model A
text: Model A includes parameters for height in both inches and centimeters, and weight in both pounds and kilograms. Think about how these variables might be related to each other.

title: Understanding Model B
text: Model B simplifies the parameters by only including height in centimeters and weight in kilograms. Consider how this might affect the confidence intervals compared to Model A.

title: Exploring Multicollinearity
text: Which model is more likely to have multicollinearity issues due to the inclusion of similar variables?

title: Confidence Intervals and Multicollinearity
text: Multicollinearity can inflate the standard errors of the coefficients, which might make the confidence intervals wider. Consider how this could affect the likelihood of the intervals containing zero.

title: Impact on Confidence Intervals
text: Given the potential multicollinearity in Model A, are the confidence intervals for its parameters more likely to contain zero compared to Model B?
